items.title: Desire's Antidote Completes: Scripture, Then the Closing Formula

items.zh: 以無量門稱揚讚歎一切貪欲永斷功德。所謂契經、應頌、記別，乃至廣說。為斷貪欲，於此正法聽聞受持，言善通利、意善尋思、見善通達，即於此法，如是宴坐，如理思惟。由是因緣，貪欲纏蓋未生不生，已生除遣。如是方便，從順障法淨修其心。
items.en: Through countless approaches, one praises and extols every merit of permanently ending desire — as set forth in discourses, verse restatements, prophecies, and so on at length. In order to cut off desire, one hears and retains this teaching, so that one's speech becomes fluent in it, one's mind investigates it well, and one's insight penetrates it thoroughly; and, relying on this very teaching, one sits in meditation and reflects correctly. By this cause, the entanglement of desire does not arise if not yet arisen, and is removed if already arisen. Such are the skilful means by which the mind is purified of what accords with the obstructions.

items.title: Section: Ill-Will's Antidote — Boundless Loving-Kindness in All Directions

items.zh: 於瞋恚蓋法有差別者，謂如是宴坐，以慈俱心，無怨無敵、無損無惱，廣大無量，極善修習；普於一方發起勝解，具足安住。如是第二、如是第三、如是第四，上下傍布，普遍一切無邊世界發起勝解，具足安住。餘如前說。
items.en: Regarding the distinct method for the hindrance of ill-will: one sits in meditation with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness — free of resentment, free of hostility, free of the wish to harm, free of malice — vast and boundless, cultivated to the utmost, and, directed pervasively towards one direction, gives rise to a resolute understanding, abiding in it fully. So too towards the second direction, the third, the fourth, and above, below, and the intermediate points, pervading all boundless worlds, giving rise to that same resolute understanding, abiding in it fully. The rest is as explained before.

items.title: Restlessness-and-Remorse's Antidote: The Nine Stages of Mental Abiding

items.zh: 於掉舉惡作蓋法有差別者，謂如是宴坐，令心內住，成辦一趣，得三摩地。餘如前說。
items.en: Regarding the distinct method for the hindrance of restlessness and remorse: one sits in meditation causing the mind to abide inwardly, to become one-pointed, and to attain concentration. The rest is as explained before.

items.title: Section: Doubt's Antidote — Rejecting Speculation, Reflecting Rightly on Dependent Origination

items.zh: 於疑蓋法有差別者，謂如是宴坐，於過去世，非不如理作意思惟；於未來世、於現在世，非不如理作意思惟。我於過去為曾有耶？為曾無耶？我於過去為曾何有？云何曾有？我於未來為當何有？云何當有？我於現在為何所有？云何而有？今此有情從何而來？於此殞沒當往何所？於如是等不如正理作意思惟，應正遠離。如理思惟去來今世，唯見有法，唯見有事；知有為有，知無為無；唯觀有因，唯觀有果；於實無事不增不益，於實有事不毀不謗。於其實有，了知實有。謂於無常、苦、空、無我一切法中，了知無常、苦、空、無我。以能如是如理思惟，便於佛所無惑無疑。餘如前說。
items.en: Regarding the distinct method for the hindrance of doubt: sitting in meditation, one does not engage in incorrect reflection about the past, the future, or the present. Did I exist in the past, or did I not? … Where does this being come from, and where will it go once it perishes here? Such incorrect reflection should rightly be avoided. Reflecting correctly on the past, future, and present, one sees only phenomena, only events; one knows what exists as existing, and what does not exist as not existing; one observes only causes and only effects; one neither exaggerates what is truly non-existent nor denies what is truly existent. Regarding what truly exists, one understands it as it truly is — namely, understanding impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self within all phenomena as impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self. By reflecting correctly in this way, one comes to have no confusion and no doubt regarding the Buddha. The rest is as explained before.

items.title: Doubt's Antidote Closes, and "Purifying the Mind by the Power of the Teaching" Concludes

items.zh: 於法、於僧、於苦、於集、於滅、於道、於因，及因所生諸法無惑無疑。餘如前說。又於瞋恚蓋應作是說：為斷瞋恚及瞋恚相，於此正法聽聞受持，乃至廣說。於掉舉惡作蓋應作是說：為斷掉舉惡作及順彼法，於此正法聽聞受持，乃至廣說。於其疑蓋應作是說：為斷疑蓋及順彼法，於此正法聽聞受持，乃至廣說。如是方便，從貪欲、瞋恚、惛沈睡眠、掉舉惡作、疑蓋，及順彼法，淨修其心。是故說言：經行、宴坐，從順障法淨修其心。如是已說由法增上，從順障法淨修其心。
items.en: Regarding the Dharma, the Saṅgha, suffering, its origin, its cessation, the path, cause, and the phenomena arising from cause, one has no confusion and no doubt. …And regarding the hindrance of ill-will, it should likewise be said: in order to cut off ill-will and its mark, one hears and retains this teaching, and so on at length. Regarding the hindrance of restlessness and remorse, it should likewise be said: in order to cut off restlessness and remorse and what accords with them, one hears and retains this teaching, and so on at length. Regarding the hindrance of doubt, it should likewise be said: in order to cut off doubt and what accords with it, one hears and retains this teaching, and so on at length. By such skilful means, the mind is purified of desire, ill-will, sloth-and-torpor, restlessness-and-remorse, doubt, and what accords with them. It is therefore said: through walking and sitting meditation, the mind is purified of what accords with the obstructions.

items.title: Section: A Second Power — Purifying the Mind Through One's Own Conscience

items.zh: 復有由自增上及世增上、從順障法淨修其心。云何名為由自增上？謂如有一，於諸蓋中隨起一種，便自了知此非善法，於所生蓋不堅執著，速疾棄捨、擯遣、變吐。又能自觀此所生蓋，甚可羞恥，令心染惱，令慧羸劣，是損害品。如是名為由自增上，從順障法淨修其心。
items.en: Furthermore, there is purifying the mind of what accords with the obstructions through one's own conscience and through concern for the world. What is meant by one's own conscience? It is like one who, when any one of the hindrances arises, immediately recognises it as unwholesome, does not cling firmly to the hindrance that has arisen, and swiftly abandons it, casts it out, and expels it. Such a one further observes that the hindrance which has arisen is truly shameful — it defiles the mind and weakens wisdom, and is thus a harmful thing. This is called purifying the mind of what accords with the obstructions through one's own conscience.

items.title: A Third Power: Purifying the Mind Through Concern for Others' Regard

items.zh: 云何名為由世增上，從順障法淨修其心？謂如有一，於諸蓋中隨一已生，或將生時，便作是念：我若生起所未生蓋，當為大師之所訶責，亦為諸天及諸有智同梵行者以法輕毀。彼由如是世增上故，未生諸蓋能令不生，已生諸蓋能速棄捨。如是名為由世增上，從順障法淨修其心。
items.en: What is meant by purifying the mind of what accords with the obstructions through concern for the world? It is like one who, when any one of the hindrances has arisen or is about to arise, thinks: if I allow a hindrance not yet arisen to arise, I will be reproached by the Teacher, and will be rightly disdained by the gods and by wise companions in the spiritual life. Through this concern for the world, hindrances not yet arisen are prevented from arising, and hindrances already arisen are swiftly abandoned. This is called purifying the mind of what accords with the obstructions through concern for the world.

blocks.text: The remaining antidotes in sitting meditation, and three "powers" that purify the mind. A short passage (0412b05–c27) is fully translated.
Venerable Miào Jìng: "you cannot just close your eyes and practise calm and insight; you must also recite the scriptures and treatises."

"One sits with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, free of resentment, hostility, the wish to harm," pervading the first direction, then the second, and so on through all directions. It is the antidote to ill will.

Against restlessness and remorse: "causing the mind to abide inwardly, to become one-pointed, to attain concentration": the nine stages of mental abiding (to be explained in detail in fascicle 30). Master Cháng Bǎi: equipoise, the last stage, is effortless.

"Where did this being come from, and where will it go when it perishes here?" Such reflection, assuming a self, should be avoided. Instead one reflects on dependent origination: only causes and effects, without denying causes (Venerable Miào Jìng: "denying") or effects ("disparaging"). Master Cháng Bǎi: one sees only projecting and producing causes, and their results.

Besides the power of the teaching, two more powers purify the mind. **One's own**: when a hindrance arises, "one recognises it as unwholesome, does not cling to it, casts it out". Venerable Miào Jìng: casting out stops its activity; expelling discards its seed. **The world's**: "If I allow a hindrance to arise, I will be reproached by the Teacher, and disdained by the gods and wise companions." Venerable Miào Jìng: these are simply shame (慚) and embarrassment (愧).

quiz.q: The text says to hear and retain the teaching and then sit and reflect on it. What does Venerable Miào Jìng stress here?
options: sitting with eyes closed is enough
one must not only close one's eyes and meditate; one must also recite the scriptures and treatises
reading is enough; no need to sit
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: you cannot just close your eyes and practice calm and insight; you must also recite the scriptures and treatises.

quiz.q: How does one meditate to counter the hindrance of ill-will?
options: with a mind of loving-kindness, free of resentment and hostility, vast and boundless, pervading one direction with resolute understanding
quiz.why: "One sits in meditation with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness — free of resentment, free of hostility, free of the wish to harm, free of malice — vast and boundless." Venerable Miào Jìng: loving-kindness is a mental factor accompanying the mind, hence "a mind accompanied by loving-kindness."

quiz.q: How does one sit to counter restlessness and remorse, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng link this to?
options: make the mind abide inwardly, become one-pointed, and attain concentration; the nine stages of mental abiding
quiz.why: "One sits in meditation causing the mind to abide inwardly, to become one-pointed, and to attain concentration." Venerable Miào Jìng: inner abiding here is the nine stages — inner, even, firm, close abiding, taming, calming, utter calming, one-pointedness, and equipoise.

quiz.q: To counter doubt, what kind of reflection should be avoided, and where does Master Cháng Bǎi say doubt comes from?
options: reflecting on the Buddha's virtues; from faith
incorrect reflection like "where does this being come from and go?"; from not understanding non-self in the three times
quiz.why: "Where does this being come from, and where will it go once it perishes here? Such incorrect reflection should rightly be avoided." Master Cháng Bǎi: doubt arises from not understanding non-self in the past, present, and future.

quiz.q: Which two causes and two effects does Master Cháng Bǎi see in "one observes only causes and only effects"?
options: good and bad causes; pleasant and painful effects
father and mother; male and female
near and far causes; big and small effects
projecting and producing causes; the effect of one's own body and the effect of the experienced world
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one sees only two kinds of cause — projecting and producing — and two kinds of effect — the effect of one's own existence and the effect of the experienced world.

quiz.q: To what two words do both masters reduce "one's own conscience" and "concern for the world"?
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: one's own conscience and concern for the world are, in truth, just the two words "shame" and "embarrassment before others." Master Cháng Bǎi likewise: the first is shame, the second embarrassment before others.

quiz.q: Under concern for the world, one fears being "reproached by the Teacher." Who is the Teacher, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: the Buddha — one would be rebuked by the Buddha
quiz.why: "If I allow a hindrance not yet arisen to arise, I will be reproached by the Teacher, and will be rightly disdained by the gods and by wise companions in the spiritual life." Venerable Miào Jìng: who is the Teacher? The Buddha — one would be rebuked by the Buddha.
